The internal disequilibrium, in its turn, cannot be overcome unless the appropriation, accumulation and distribution of income are radically transformed by means of macroeconomic regulation of the global surplus through a democratic process in which all social groups take part, in particular those which have been left without a share in the fruits of development.-from Journal summary © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: D., Ibarra, D.
Title: Crisis, adjustment and economic policy in Latin America.
Authors with affiliations: Ibarra, D.,
Abstract: Asserts that many of the central problems which look like conjunctural distortions in reality stem from imperfect structural adjustments both in the international economy and within the Latin American countries, the treatment and cure of which will be much more than a short term matter. To all this is added a set of circumstances which hinder the application of appropriate solutions, such as the decline in the industrialized centres' ability to provide development aid, and the undermining of the leadership capacity of governments by the doubts cast on the commitment to guarantee sustained growth. The answers are to be found in the political sphere, because only there could the foundations be laid for the social consensuses which would enable state and society to join in a national commitment with the aim of regaining self-determination and access to development.-from Journal summary English © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: M., Mortimore, M.
Title: The subsidiary role of direct foreign investment in industrialization: the Colombian manufacturing sector.
Authors with affiliations: Mortimore, M.,
Abstract: In national industrialization processes, direct foreign investment, together with the incorporation of new technologies, enables the modernization of industry to go hand in hand with the promotion of its development. However, the goals of the transnational corporations do not always coincide with the economic policy objectives of the host State. Hence, almost all the governments of the region have set up, in varying measure, administrative systems to assess, authorize, register, and occasionally supervise foreign participation. There is always some tension between the aims of modernization, with its reduced control and restriction of the activities of the transnational corporations, and national participation, which implies more supervision. The importance of the Colombian case lies in the way in which it resolved this tension by assigning a subsidiary role to foreign participation, particularly in the industrial field. To verify the impact of this policy, a survey was made of the 26 largest firms in the manufacturing sector in which foreign participation was involved.-from Journal summary © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: E., Lahera, E.
Title: The transnational corporation and Latin America's international trade.
Authors with affiliations: Lahera, E.,
Abstract: The transnational corporations have a high potential for internationalizing their productive process, which would lead to the expectation of a large volume of external trade from them. However, the vast majority of their sales in Latin America are made in the various national markets. This paradox is explained by the fact that direct foreign investment in the countries was made in order to take advantage of different types of protectionism. The most important exception has been in the extractive sectors, control of which has gradually been transferred to local investors. Nevertheless, the aggregate figures conceal important differences. In some countries the transnational corporations have made a positive contribution to the trade balance, have opened new export markets or developed new lines of exportable products, and their participation in the processes of regional integration has been noteworthy. The main explanation of the differences observed lies in public policies.-from Journal summary © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: M., Figueroa, M.
Title: Rural development and urban food programming.
Authors with affiliations: Figueroa, M.,
Abstract: Rapid urban growth, the persistence of the agrarian question, the obstinacy of marketing problems, and the relative lack of state intervention in the market are some of the causes of the present complex situation of the urban food supply. The second part presents those factors that should be considered in designing an urban food supply strategy, which include marketing, the placement of human settlements, energy, collective consumption patterns, food education, hygiene, soil use, nutrition, and economic policy measures, for times of crisis and for the medium and long term. In the third part, discusses the problems of the articulation of the institutional and administrative apparatus associated with such a strategy. Finally, restates the conviction that the urban food supply can only be effectively organized if the producers and consumers affected by its shortcomings band together and pressure for far-reaching changes in these structures.-from Journal summary © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: T.S., Di Tella, Torcuato S.
Title: The political and social outlook for Latin America.
Affiliations: Universidad de Buenos Aires, Buenos Aires, Argentina
Authors with affiliations: Di Tella, Torcuato S., Universidad de Buenos Aires, Buenos Aires, Argentina
Abstract: Sketches the broad outlines of a strategy for stimulating medium- and long-term development. As regards the external debt, forecasts an increasingly conflictive situation, to the point at which its seriousness will lead to the acceptance of more flexible proposals by the creditor banks and countries. Against this background, the Latin American countries must reorient their economic development along the path of industrialization, protection, and planning already pointed out by some of them in the 1930s. This implies an emphasis on state intervention and on the improvement of its efficiency, the mobilization of idle resources, the orientation of production towards activities which will help to raise technoproductive, scientific, social and cultural levels, the strengthening of democratic systems and the reenforcement of regional co-operation.-from Journal summary © 2018 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: G., O'Donnell, G.
Title: External debt: why don't our governments do the obvious? ( Latin America).
Authors with affiliations: O'Donnell, G.,
Abstract: Argues for the Latin America political leadership to set out the real choices before their people, as well as the costs and risks involved in each of them. Such a dialogue, based on the patriotic and carefully considered search for a way out of the dilemma, would represent an important first step. -from Journal summary © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: F., Herrera, F.
Title: Twenty-five years ot the Inter-American Development Bank.
Authors with affiliations: Herrera, F.,
Abstract: The experience of the last 25 years in Latin America shows that international public financing, from whatever standpoint, is an essential form of co-operation for the advancement of the region. The article by its first President, Mr. Felipe Herrera, is published as a tribute to the role played by the Bank. -from Journal summary © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: The agriculture of Latin America: changes, trends and outlines of strategy.
Abstract: The first part considers changes and trends in the region's agriculture, beginning with the rapid penetration of capitalist relations of production and the formation of the two dominant types of structure: business and peasant. It also analyzes the various aspects of the evolution of the region's gross domestic farm product, and describes the impact on the sector both of the present crisis and of the policies adopted to deal with it. The second part suggests the outlines of a strategy to attain the principal objectives of elimination of rural poverty and reduction of external vulnerability with regard to food. Concludes by emphasizing the role of the State and the need to create a democratic and participatory framework. -from Journal summary © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: J.T., Zorrilla, J. T.; E., Gana, E.
Title: Trade and equilibrium among the ALADI countries ( Latin America).
Authors with affiliations: Zorrilla, J. T., ; Gana, E.,
Abstract: The Latin American economic crisis has had a powerful adverse effect on the trade flows of the ALADI countries. Nevertheless, effective co-operation among them is now more necessary than ever in order to overcome the external bottleneck and restore the levels of intra-zonal trade. The reactivation of zonal trade should, moreover, generate additional trade on a relatively more balanced and stable basis than in the past, through the multilateral linkages within the zone. Puts forward a methodology for selecting products that could potentially be traded among the countries of the zone and for determining which of those products could serve as pivots for the recovery of the trade flows. -from Journal summary © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: G., Maldonado, G.
Title: Latin America and integration: options in the crisis.
Authors with affiliations: Maldonado, G.,
Abstract: The main argument is that Latin America must strengthen its arrangements for regional co-operation and integration and make better use of its own resources; ideas, projects and processes have been set in motion for this purpose and must be given real political support. -from Journal summary © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: F.R., Fiallo, F. R.
Title: A two-front attack to overcome the payments crisis of developing countries ( debt).
Authors with affiliations: Fiallo, F. R.,
Abstract: The measures proposed relate to the establishment of an international currency based on primary products, which could be administered by the International Monetary Fund, and to the adoption by the developing countries of a more persuasive strategy in negotiations on access to markets. To implement the measures the developing countries would need to assume an active role, inasmuch as they would have to turn their own natural resources and import markets to account, manipulating them as bases for negotiations. This two-front attack would improve the power of the developing countries to negotiate debt maturities and terms of payment and would also considerably lighten the burden of the adjustment programmes which the countries are adopting. -from Journal summary © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: J.E., Navarrete, J. E.
Title: Foreign policy and international financial negotiations: the external debt and the Cartagena Consensus.
Authors with affiliations: Navarrete, J. E.,
Abstract: The background, development, and prospects of the concerted effort being made by the Latin American countries as expressed in the Cartagena Consensus and Mexico's role in this effort are discussed. An attempt is made to explore those elements of international economic performance, trade, and finance which led the Latin American countries to meet at Cartagena. It analyzes the basic content of the proposals made at that meeting and at Mar del Plata and Santo Domingo, to discuss how the other parties to the negotiations have reacted to these proposals, and, finally, to describe what the outlook for the overall Cartagena process appears to be as of mid-1985. -from Journal summary © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: C., Secchi, C.
Title: On the role of small and medium-sized enterprises in the improvement of the production structure of developing countries ( industry).
Authors with affiliations: Secchi, C.,
Abstract: Focuses on the structure of the production system and on policies for improving it, with particular reference to medium-sized and small enterprises. Information and specific examples are provided based on Italy's experience. Opens with an analysis of the interplay between entrepreneurship and a firm's external environment as a basis for laying down guidelines concerning the reciprocal relationship between development and economic efficiency. A discussion of the advantages of small and medium-sized industries is followed by a description of the conditions which permit and promote their creation and growth. Concludes by discussing the role performed by these industries in the introduction of innovations and in the processes of internationalization. -Journal summary © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: R.T., Devlin, Robert T.
Title: External debt and crisis: the decline of the orthodox strategy ( Latin America).
Authors with affiliations: Devlin, Robert T.,
Abstract: Argues that the favourable trends of the terms of rescheduling was due not so much to some objective fundamental change in the image of creditworthiness of the borrowers as to their increased bargaining power, which enabled them to capture the monopoly rents obtained by the banks in the initial rounds of negotiation. Goes on to analyze the North-South debate on the heavy transfer of resources from the region to the creditor banks, concluding that this cannot be justified by the conventional criteria of economic theory. Finally, within the framework of the bilateral monopoly, the study suggests various options that would permit the countries to reduce the transfer to the banks and thus give greater support to their own growth and development. -from Journal summary © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: E., Sarmiento, E.
Title: The imperfections of the capital market.
Authors with affiliations: Sarmiento, E.,
Abstract: Part I identifies some outstanding elements which have not been explicitly incorporated into the analysis of the capital market. In part II the effects of the liberalization of the capital markets are examined, while part III discusses how far the information given in part II corroborates the assumptions of the capital market behaviour presented in part I. In addition, these elements are analyzed simultaneously in order to synthesize the causes of the imperfections in the capital market and their relation to financial liberalization. The final part outlines the features of the financial reforms required to achieve the reconciliation of efficiency with stability. -from Journal summary © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: B., Gosovic, B.
Title: Population - resources - environment - development interrelationships in the United Nations: in search of an approach.
Authors with affiliations: Gosovic, B.,
Abstract: Deals with the manner in which the problem presents itself in the United Nations and probes the basic dimensions of this complex, polemical topic of international concern and discourse. -from Journal summaryECLA/UNEP Env & Dev Unit, Santiago, Chile. © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: G.W., Rama, Germán W.
Title: Education in Latin America. Exclusion or participation.
Authors with affiliations: Rama, Germán W.,
Abstract: Alludes to the educational model proper, to the colonial system and to its perpetuation. Deals with the existing contradictions between social practice and expositions of principle, analysing characteristics proper to the region in terms of educational supply and demand. Analyzes the form taken by the development of education during the last three decades, questioning the contradiction between the expectations focused on education and the real possibilities of upward social mobility. Propounds four socio-educational models: exclusive, classist, segmentary, and universalist, with the aim of encompassing the diversity of historical situations existing in the region. -from Author © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: M., Wolfe, M.
Title: Styles of development and education. A stocktaking of myths, prescriptions and potentialities.
Authors with affiliations: Wolfe, M.,
Abstract: Sets forth the principles on which the transformation of the educational models and conditions should be based. Appraises some recent experiences in educational reform and considers the significance of non-formal education. Examines the role that could be played by three important 'clienteles' of the educational system in the event of its reform: young, university-educated persons, teachers, and the poor or excluded. As regards future trends, takes the view that neither a situation of stable continuism nor one of thorough-going change will prevail, but rather policies of 'crisis management' whose consequences are very difficult to anticipate. -from Author © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: C.H., Filgueira, C. H.
Title: To educate or not to educate: is that the question ( Latin America)?
Authors with affiliations: Filgueira, C. H.,
Abstract: Looks at the way in which education has contributed to social mobility, particularly in Latin America; examines internal trends in educational stratification, the social bases of educational recruitment, and the practical efficacy of formal education in relation to mobility. This analysis leads to the conclusion that education is at present passing through a critical phase, since it has ceased to be a medium for the absorption of pressures and demands on the part of the social groups and has become a source of fresh conflicts. This must be ascribed to the presence of two contradictory trends: the enormous expansion of the educational system, and the very limited absorption of the new contingents by the economic system, with the ensuing detriment to structural mobility. Social conflict regarding access to education will probably be exacerbated as relative overeducation increases and the value of educational achievements declines. -from Author © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: P., Demo, P.
Title: Education and culture: a political perspective. Hypotheses on the importance of education for development.
Authors with affiliations: Demo, P.,
Abstract: Argues that if education is to be able to fulfil its role as a means of occupational insertion and a channel of social mobility, the economic structure must be expanded and new opportunities must really be created. Education can also be justified by its role as an instrument of socialization, although there are two sides to this: positive, in so far as it furnishes knowledge with which to face life, and negative, in so far as it makes for moulding individuals in conformity with the social system. Asserts that its most important role lies in the political formation of educands, whereby they can become citizens participating in an increasingly democratic society. Concludes with the proposition that the educational system be changed in such a way that its expansion may create a climate in which a free and democratic society can flourish. -from Author © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: C.A., Borsotti, C. A.
Title: Development and education in rural areas.
Authors with affiliations: Borsotti, C. A.,
Abstract: The problems connected with education in rural areas fall into four categories: 1) 'preliminary questions', relating in particular to the normative and technical principles on the basis of which the existing situation is interpreted and proposals for action are formulated; 2) the application of these principles to decisions bearing on what for, for whom, in what form, and how education is to be provided; 3) the conditions in which educational policies are put into practice; 4) the status of society and education in rural areas. The problems falling within this fourth and last category are discussed in the second half, which aims to present a picture of the structures of rural society, of the changes that have taken place during the last few decades, and of some particularly important aspects of education in rural areas. Concludes that in a time of crisis it is unlikely that these will be able to compete successfully with other more powerful areas and groups for the scanty resources available. -from Author © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: J.C., Tedesco, Juan Carlos
Title: Pedagogical model and school failure.
Authors with affiliations: Tedesco, Juan Carlos,
Abstract: Divides the causes for school failure into various types: material exogenous causes are connected in particular with socioeconomic conditions and family structure; cultural exogenous causes, with family attitudes and values vis-a-vis education, linguistic patterns, and mass communication media; material endogenous causes, with school resources and endowments and the organization of the school system; and cultural endogenous causes, with teaching methods, content and orientation, and the training and attitudes of teachers. After reviewing the main research on the subject conducted in Latin America, concludes that there is no solid evidence to support the unidimensional predominance of any type. Recommends that further research on key aspects should be undertaken, and that the orientation of policy measures bearing on school failures should be decided upon without a priori dismissal of some of the types of causes mentioned. -from Author © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.
Author Keywords: Education; Latin America

Authors: G., Weinberg, G.
Title: A historical perspective of Latin American education.
Authors with affiliations: Weinberg, G.,
Abstract: Aims to justify on the one hand the validity and interest of the historical dimension and, on the other, the use of categories of analysis such as development 'models' or 'styles'. The period of time covered, two centuries, reveals that both the prevailing conditions and the educational ideas display very different features and characteristics depending on the countries and circumstances, and many of them still persist. Indicates that overcoming many of the present maladjustments, contradictions, or shortcomings of the educational system or of the relations between this system and society calls for studies to prepare models which are technically satisfactory and viable in practice. -from Author © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: J.P., Terra, Juan Pablo
Title: The role of education in relation to employment problems ( Latin America).
Authors with affiliations: Terra, Juan Pablo,
Abstract: The first part reviews the controversy on unemployment and underemployment problems in Latin America, their nature and causes, and the measures which should be applied to eradicate them. Emphasizes the importance of the concept of structural heterogeneity in the description and interpretation of these problems, and of the criticism of the economistic conception which assumes that their solution consists simply in increasing the rate of economic growth. Part two focuses on the relation between education and employment; its central thesis is that the most important problems of both are closely linked to the economic, social, cultural, and political segmentation of society and that the interpretation of these problems and the policies must therfore take into consideration this fact. Argues that education's major problem today does not derive from its supposed overexpansion but from the inequality that has characterized its distribution by social strata, geographical areas, and sex, and the consequently limited access to it observable in some disadvantaged social groups. -from Author © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: M., Guerguil, M.
Title: The international financial crisis: diagnoses and prescriptions.
Authors with affiliations: Guerguil, M.,
Abstract: There are those that assume that the payment difficulties of the debtor countries are an expression of a conjunctural and transitory situation which will terminate with the recovery of the world economy. In these circumstances, the proper course is to amplify and improve existing mechanisms that will assist the debtor countries in the short term servicing of their external debt, as for examle by increasing the resources of international financing sources, improving the temporary relief mechanisms and reorienting the conditionality criterion of the IMF. On the other hand, there are those who maintain that the difficulties stem from the serious mismanagement of international credit and that a system should be devised that would avoid a repetition of the errors of the past, restructure the debt overhang and redistribute more equitably the costs of readjustment between the parties involved. Concludes that the creditor banks and countries are obtaining handsome benefits from the existing situation, so that they cannot be expected to want to change it; hence, any attempts to establish new bases for the problem of external indebtedness will largely depend on the bargaining power that can be built up and applied by the debtor countries.-from Journal summary © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: A., Dorfman, A.
Title: The structural crisis in Argentine industry.
Authors with affiliations: Dorfman, A.,
Abstract: Outlines the main trends in Argentine industrial development, and discusses the problems which they entail. In so doing, reviews the evolution of the industrial product in recent decades and the gaps which exist in the structure of this sector, its increasing technological progress, the drop in industrial employment occasioned by industrial modernization and by the production slump of recent years, the concentration of economic power in industry and the increasing role of foreign capital, the persistent geographic centralization of the sector, and the expansion of industrial exports. Suggests a combination of high-technology capital- intensive companies with more labour-intensive medium-sized and small enterprises, along with a thorough assessment of the part played by foreign capital.-from Journal summary © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: M., Wolfe, M.
Title: Participation: the view from above.
Affiliations: UNRISD, Geneve, Switzerland
Authors with affiliations: Wolfe, M., UNRISD, Geneve, Switzerland
Abstract: The central thesis is that political processes in which participation is encouraged will always be attended by a permanent tension between their main protagonists, in particular the state, progressivist movements, and the people. After an analysis of the concepts of development and participation, discusses the controversial issues of accumulation and consumption, planning and the market, conflict and consensus between social classes, local and national forms of participation and solidarity, the role of bureaucrats and technocrats and the tension between them and participation, and the national character of development processes. Lastly, a set of recommendations are outlined in terms of the attitudes or predispositions to be desired in agents of the state, ideologists, and intermediaries between the state, and the popular movements, in order to further the participation of the excluded groups. -from Journal summary © 2018 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: C., Massad, C.; R., Zahler, R.
Title: The adjustment process in the 1980s: the need for a global approach.
Authors with affiliations: Massad, C., ; Zahler, R.,
Abstract: New approaches for Latin America emerge which make it possible to minimize the domestic costs of the adjustment process and to achieve results favourable to the world economy as a whole. These approaches involve drawing a distinction between recessive adjustment and expansive adjustment: the former consists in bringing about a reduction in the level of economic activity and imports, whereas the latter seeks to raise the level of employment and activity by increasing exports. A set of measures is proposed for improving the adjustment process and lessening the negative impact on the developing countries of the economic policies adopted in the industrialized countries.-from Journal summary © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: L., Tomassini, L.
Title: The international scene and Latin America's external debt.
Authors with affiliations: Tomassini, L.,
Abstract: The international economic crisis which began in the late 1960s put an end to the record cycle of expansion that the industrialized countries had enjoyed during the previous 20 years and facilitated the rise in oil prices, which generated large surpluses of liquid assets. Some developing countries, among them the largest Latin American nations, advanced rapidly towards an intermediate stage of development and integrated themselves more closely into the international economy. Thus they could exploit opportunities and assume risks to a much greater extent than in the past, which explains the great impact of the current crisis on the Latin American countries.-from Journal summary © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: R.L., Ground, R. L.
Title: Orthodox adjustment programmes in Latin America: a critical look at the policies of the International Monetary Fund.
Affiliations: Comisión Económica para América Latina y el Caribe, Santiago, Chile
Authors with affiliations: Ground, R. L., Econ Dev Div, Comisión Económica para América Latina y el Caribe, Santiago, Chile
Abstract: Analyzes the orthodox adjustment paradigm, as well as recent suggestions for including in it consideration of certain structural factors, and discusses the recessionary bias that is inherent in that paradigm. This bias is evident both in the meagre and belated financial support given the Latin Amerian countries by the IMF during the current crisis, and in the domestic policies provided for in the adjustment programmes it recommends. -from Journal summary © 2018 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: N., Garcia, N.; V.E., Tokman, Victor E.
Title: Changes in employment and the crisis.
Authors with affiliations: Garcia, N., ; Tokman, Victor E.,
Abstract: The first part of the article describes the changes in the structure of employment between 1950 and 1980, re-examines some of the interpretations that have been made and highlights the diversity of situations found in the various countries of the region. The second concentrates on the effects that the present crisis has produced on employment, above all the increases in open unemployment, visible and invisible underemployment, and the fall in real wages. Concludes that during recent decades Latin America was slowly overcoming its employment problems and transforming its employment structure, while at the same time undergoing rapid urbanization; but it was doing so in a heterogeneous framework in which modern urban employment increased while underemployment persisted. The current crisis has been a serious obstacle to the productive absorption of labour and has impaired the levels of income and standards of living, thereby converting employment into one of the most outstanding and intractable economic and political problems of the present time.-from Journal summary © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: R., Kaztman, R.
Title: Sectoral transformations in employment in Latin America.
Authors with affiliations: Kaztman, R.,
Abstract: Analyzes the available statistical data in order to contribute to the interpretation of the process of absorptioin of labour in Latin America over the last 30 years. With regard to agriculture, some evidence is offered concerning the changes in the relationships of production which accompanied the sharp decline in agriculture's relative share of the total labour force. In considering the transformations in industry, it examines the view that maintains that this sector is incapable of absorbing labour at a rate that can cope with the magnitude of the growth of the non-agricultural active population and, in the analysis of the tertiary sector, it explains the nature of the sector's remarkable expansion from 1950.-from Journal summary © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: D., Cordovez, D.
Title: Institutional elements of a new diplomacy for development (notes for a book of memoirs).
Authors with affiliations: Cordovez, D.,
Abstract: Analyzes the main features of the new diplomacy for development begun with the first UNCTAD session in 1964 and the way in which it has evolved up to the present deadlock situation. This situation derives from the existence of a sharp conflict of interests, either real or perceived, between the developed and developing countries, but it has also been aggravated by a number of institutional problems. Outstanding among these are the proliferation of organs and forums which are often in conflict with each other; the negative effects of the efforts to maintain the unity of the 2 major blocs; the large number of participants in the negotiations, and finally a certain degree of incoherence in the positions of individual governments in different forums. Stresses the need to break the current deadlock in the North-South dialogue, and suggests some measures.-from Journal summary © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: J., Ramos, J.
Title: Urbanization and the labour market.
Authors with affiliations: Ramos, J.,
Abstract: Examines the way in which rapid demographic growth was absorbed in the labour market, especially when it turned towards the towns, argues that this increase in the supply of labour found an outlet in the accompanying increase in demand, with productive employment being created as a result of the region's rapid economic growth over the last decades. Since 1980 Latin America has been undergoing an acute economic crisis which is reversing this trend, confirming how sensitive employment is to economic growth rates. Concludes, therefore, that concentrated and heterogeneous growth like that of 1950-1980 does create problems, but many fewer than those produced by the kind of economic recession experienced in recent years.- from Journal summary © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: A., Couriel, Alberto
Title: Poverty and underemployment in Latin America.
Authors with affiliations: Couriel, Alberto,
Abstract: Shows that during the period 1950-1980, despite the intense economic growth and the high rate of labour absorption in urban areas, the level of underemployment remained almost constant, although the greater proportion is now urban and not rural as in the past. There are two main factors that account for this trend: population growth and rural-urban migrations, and, the content or type of the economic growth. This latter is the more important, comprising in particular the predominant forms of international insertion of the Latin American countries and the styles of industrial and agrarian development adopted by them in recent decades. These features explain the high but insufficient absorption of the urban labour force, the scant increase in the manpower employed in the modern agricultural sector, and the persistence of small peasant farmers (minifundistas). These structural problems call for solutions centered on the transformation of the productive structure and the pattern of external insertion.-from Journal summary English © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: A., Di Filippo, A.
Title: Social use of the surplus, accumulation, and distribution and employment.
Authors with affiliations: Di Filippo, A.,
Abstract: Explores the structural heterogeneity and the insufficient dynamism of Latin American societies, with special reference to the use they have chiefly made of the surplus. Postulates that the global surplus represents a very high proportion of income, but the pace and orientations of accumulation do not suffice to redeem the labour force subsisting in the lower strata from the depths of intolerable poverty. As a counterpart, over-consumption of the surplus increases social inequalities and promotes the imitation of life styles, which correspond to much higher levels of productivity and income.-from Journal summary English © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: E.V., Iglesias, E. V.
Title: Latin America: crisis and development options.
Affiliations: Comisión Económica para América Latina y el Caribe, Santiago, Chile
Authors with affiliations: Iglesias, E. V., Comisión Económica para América Latina y el Caribe, Santiago, Chile
Abstract: The purpose of the first and second sections is to identify the origins and the special characteristics of the crisis and the decisive part played in it by the external debt, the markedly recessive adjustment policies that have been applied, and the costs and tensions which they have engendered. The third section refers to the immediate prospects, which do not seem overpromising, while the fourth discusses the medium-term outlook and its main external and internal determinants. The last section sketches policy options that could be pursued, with due regard to the considerable inter- country differences existent. It underlines the priority objectives towards which these policies should be oriented: economic efficiency and growth, equity in the distribution of the benefits of such growth, and autonomy in development.-from Journal summary © 2018 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Productive absorption of the labour force: an ongoing controversy.
Abstract: A number of studies have been carried out in recent years to find out how the Latin American economies have performed in this respect. The findings are not yet conclusive and the controversy between the different points of view is in full swing. On the one hand, many economies of the region have clearly shown the ability to absorb labour productively, but on the other there is also a notable persistence of high levels of unemployment. At the same time, preliminary employment figures for 1980 are becoming available from the population censuses, enabling employment trends to be assessed from a longer-term perspective.-from Journal summary © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: A., Pinto, A.
Title: Metropolization and tertiarization: structural distortions in Latin American development.
Authors with affiliations: Pinto, A.,
Abstract: Stresses metropolitan gigantism and spurious tertiarization. These phenomena are expressions of a structural distortion in Latin American economies, whose underlying cause is the unequal social distribution of the means of production, of power and of income, which shapes the structure of supply, the sectoral distribution of the labour force and the spatial location of the population. The enormous difficulties placed by this strucural distortion in the way of productive absorption of underemployed and unemployed manpower are aggravated by the present crisis, the high rate of population growth, and the minimal absorption capacity of modern technology. Since the current possibilities of absorption in the metropolises are so slight, the occupational retention capacity of smaller nuclei and of agricultural activities must be increased, but that requires, inter alia, redistribution of land and priority resource reallocation, apart from new urban-rural patterns.-from Journal summary © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: V.E., Tokman, Victor E.
Title: Global monetarism and destruction of industry.
Affiliations: International Labour Organization, Geneva, Switzerland
Authors with affiliations: Tokman, Victor E., Regional Employment Program for Latin America and the Caribbean (PREALC), International Labour Organization, Geneva, Switzerland
Abstract: Asserts that global monetarist policies have introduced an anti-industrial bias which has diminished the importance of the sector and, in some cases, has even destroyed a large part of its installed capacity. To analyse this process, a study is made of the recent experience of Argentina since 1974 and of Chile since 1973. Some outlines are proposed for an interpretative model whereby the characteristics of a possible process of recovery can be analyzed, together with its requisities in terms of investment and employment.-from Journal summary © 2018 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: R., Prebisch, R.
Title: The crisis of capitalism and international trade.
Authors with affiliations: Prebisch, R.,
Abstract: Begins by analysing the internal structural imbalance of the centres, which consists of the disparity between the growth rate of consumption and that of the accumulation of productive capital. Then deals with the structural imbalance between the periphery and the centres, in respect to the persistent problems of trade relations between them, and the conjunctural incidence of the crisis on the peripheral countries. Finally stresses the importance currently assumed by the ideological crisis, the complex manner in which it mingles with the other aspects of the crisis, and the need to overcome the state of intellectual dependence in which the periphery has lived in recent years.-from Author © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: E.V., Iglesias, E. V.
Title: Reflections on the Latin American economy in 1982.
Authors with affiliations: Iglesias, E. V.,
Abstract: Emphasizes the incidence of external factors, especially the contraction of the developed countries' demand for imports and the rise in interest rates. The problems of external indebtedness are also analyzed, in which the author describes the situation towards the close of 1982 and expounds its causes, in particular the prolonged international recession, the high cost of credit, the negative effects of development strategies based on external borrowing, and the weaknesses of the international financial system. Lastly, recommends a policy to promote international trade and facilitate payment of the Latin American countries' external debt, but also calls for renewed efforts at regional and international cooperation amongst LDCs. -from Author © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.
Author Keywords: Credit; Debt; International Financial System

Authors: J., Katz, J.
Title: Technological change in the Latin American metal working industry: results of a programme of case studies.
Affiliations: IDB/ECLA/IDRC/UNDP Research Programme on Scientific & Technological Development in L.A.
Authors with affiliations: Katz, J., Director, IDB/ECLA/IDRC/UNDP Research Programme on Scientific & Technological Development in L.A.
Abstract: The plants manufacturing metal products and machinery in the region are far from constituting a replica of their counterparts in developed countries. Both the production processes and the organization of production predominant in Latin America differ significantly from those observable in the same fields of activity in mature industrial countries. There are also yawning gaps between the various Latin American countries, reflecting the wide diversity of situations existing in the region. Hence, a careful microeconomic scanning of different sub-branches of the metalworking industry in different Latin American countries must be made before any formulation or implementation of economic and technological policy. -from Author © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: G., Maldonado, G.; E., Gana, E.; A., Di Filippo, A.
Title: Latin America: crisis, cooperation and development.
Authors with affiliations: Maldonado, G., ; Gana, E., ; Di Filippo, A.,
Abstract: Argues that the structural resolution of the problem of peripheral status implies restoring the economic and social development of each and all of the Latin American countries to the central place that is due to it in the action taken by the State, by entrepreneurs and by the other social agents. The world order has entered upon a period of uncertainty which looks likely to be prolonged, and the Latin American countries must find a way to evade the danger of fragmentation and isolation by stepping up their efforts on behalf of regional cooperation and integration. The lethargy into which economic integration programmes have lapsed today is not attributable to 'an instrumental crisis' but, in essence, to the slackening of the drive for industrial development and the recent phase of international financial permissiveness, which has sustained the equally fleeting development styles founded on international borrowing.-Authors © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: E., Lahera, E.; H., Nochteff, H.
Title: Microelectronics and Latin American development.
Authors with affiliations: Lahera, E., ; Nochteff, H.,
Abstract: Maintains that the action of the Latin American countries with respect to microelectronics should be aimed at overcoming the exogeneous nature of the present form of incorporation of such technology. Efforts should be made to reverse the passivity and lack of discrimination which currently characterize this process, orienting it instead towards the satisfaction of the region's needs. In this way, microelectronics could become an endogenous factor generating development which would permit these countries to progress more rapidly towards their goals. This endogenization should be selective, both because of the diversity of national situations and goals and because of the disparity of resources and the impossibility of achieving simultaneous development in all aspects of such technology. -from Authors © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: R.T., Devlin, Robert T.
Title: Renegotiation of Latin America's debt: an analysis of the monopoly power of private banks.
Authors with affiliations: Devlin, Robert T.,
Abstract: The financial market has been left in the hands of a few large international banks leading to a deterioration of credit terms and a rise in the cost of borrowing. This study maintains that this increase in the cost of the debt as a result of the renegotiation is nothing but a monopoly rent which is extracted from the countries by virtue of the emergence of a non-competitive capital market. Suggests that countries should explore ways of eliminating these superprofits, because, in so far as they are rents, their non-payment should not prevent reprogramming of the debt of future access to credit.-from Author © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.
Author Keywords: Credit Terms; Financial Market; Monopoly Rent
Index Keywords: credit terms; financial market; monopoly rent

Authors: C., Alzamora T, C.; E.V., Iglesias, E. V.
Author full names: Alzamora T, C. (6506212169); Iglesias, E. V. (7004404788)
Title: Bases for a Latin American response to the international economic crisis.
Authors with affiliations: Alzamora T, C., ; Iglesias, E. V.,
Abstract: A proposal made in answer to a request from the Presendent of Ecuador, O.Hurtado, designed to develop the response capacity of Latin America and to consolidate its system of cooperation. Reviews the economic crisis affecting Latin America, and rejects the current adjustment process. Includes a call for a Latin American response at three levels, domestic, regional, and international. Internationally, it calls for concerted action on the restructuring of the debt, and regionally for the expansion of intra-Latin American trade and the establishment of a large scale dialogue to implement these actions.-P.Creese (CDS) English © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: V.E., Tokman, Victor E.
Title: Wages and employment in international recessions: recent Latin American experience.
Authors with affiliations: Tokman, Victor E.,
Abstract: Analyses the adjustment policies followed by various Latin American countries in the last two crises and concludes that if the group of countries which are so small and open that they have little autonomy in facing the crisis are omitted, the economic history of the last 5 years shows the failure both of the global monetary policies followed in the Southern Cone and of the expansive policies of the oil-exporting countries. The more eclectic models applied by other countries appear to have been most effective in reducing or at least postponing the cost of the adjustment and sharing it out more equitably. Two specific aspects are also analysed: the repercussions of the increase in interest rates on the Latin American economies, and the adjustment of the labour market, which takes different forms from one country to another.-from Author © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: C., Massad, C.
Title: The real cost of the external debt for the creditor and for the debtor.
Affiliations: Universidad de Santiago de Chile, Santiago, Chile
Authors with affiliations: Massad, C., Department of Economics, Universidad de Santiago de Chile, Santiago, Chile
Abstract: Analyzes the real cost of external debt servicing, and concludes that the cost in question is different for the creditor and for the debtor. The former will normally take into account his own country's financial market as a basis for evaluating the alternative use of his resources. In contrast, the debtor will have to take into consideration the real resources that he needs to use in his own country in order to generate foreign exchange for paying the debt. Also analyzes various factors which play a part in determining the cost of debt servicing together with the relative importance of each. The terms of trade carry the greatest weight: what is of least importance is the increment in amortization, while the effect of increases in the debt and in the interest paid varies greatly from one country to another. -from Author © 2018 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: A., Dourojeanni, Axel; M., Molina, M.
Title: The Andean peasant, water and the role of the State.
Authors with affiliations: Dourojeanni, Axel, ; Molina, M.,
Abstract: Argues that the pre-Hispanic inhabitants considered three elements as essential for proper management of water: a) the organization and coordinated participation of the community in the work; b) the use of technologies and working methods adapted to the zone; and c) control over a sufficiently large vertical and horizontal area to allow various ecological levels to be managed simultaneously. Emphasizes that the programmes in operation indicate a vast potential for the exchange of know-how through appropriate horizontal cooperation among the countries of the Andean region. -from Authors © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: A., Gurrieri, A.; P., Sainz, P.
Title: Is there a fair and democratic way out of the crisis? Some proposals in light of the ECLA philosophy ( Latin America).
Authors with affiliations: Gurrieri, A., ; Sainz, P.,
Abstract: Section I describes the main features of the crisis and makes a critical analysis of the adjustment processes now in progress; in sections II and III the form of development and the structural changes which should be carried out are set forth; in section IV the short-term policies which should be followed are examined and the final section contains some reflections on the institutional order which should govern the political process of taking decisions on the issues regarding the crisis and development. -from Authors © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: C., Massad, C.
Title: The external debt and the financial problems of Latin America.
Authors with affiliations: Massad, C.,
Abstract: Presents some data on the evolution of the total debt in the last decade to its present critical level equivalent to some 30% of the gross domestic product. Examines the reasons for this increase, dealing with them in terms of the increases in the supply of external credits and the demand for them, and emphasing changes in relative domestic prices, exchange policy, excessive public and private spending, the rise in oil prices and its impact on international liquidity, etc. Then deals with some consequences of the increase in the debt and the conditions on which this debt could be tolerable: the sustained growth of the world economy, continuity of the flow of external credit, and the expansion of exports. Suggests some emergency measures.-from AuthorEnglish © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Latin American development problems and the world economic crisis.
Abstract: A summary of the document submitted by the ECLA Secretariat to the Committee of High-Level Government Experts (CEGAN) at the latter's meeting in New York in December 1982. Part I considers the instability of the economic process, the sharp decline in the growth rate, the main economic problems, and the social tensions which the heightening of the latter is causing. Part II sets forth the main relationships between external factors and national economic processes, both from a global viewpoint and through analysis of the specific cases of Brazil, Costa Rica, Mexico, and Peru. Part III contains reflections on Latin America's future prospects and the main lines of action which could be followed in the light of the goals and objectives established in the Regional Programme of Action. -from Author © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: C.A., de Mattos, C. A.
Title: The limits of the possible in regional planning.
Authors with affiliations: de Mattos, C. A.,
Abstract: Considers the spatial implications of the formation of a national system and shows how the national systems acquire a definite spatial dynamic which leads to the formation of a particular territorial structure where the roles of each of the different subnational units are established. Lastly analyses the different factors which become restrictions on the possibilities of action in regional planning, and examines the way in which these factors limit the area for the planner.-from Author © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: K., Heynig, K.
Title: The principal schools of thought on peasant economy ( Latin America).
Authors with affiliations: Heynig, K.,
Abstract: Tries to offer a brief critical synthesis of the principal approaches to peasants, grouping them into anthropological approaches, 'modernizing' or neoclassical approaches, Marxist approaches, Chayanov's theory of the peasant economy and other aspects of the contemporary debate in Latin America. Suggests future work on peasant agriculture.-from Author © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: J.W., Durston, John W.
Title: Class and culture in the changing peasantry ( Latin America).
Authors with affiliations: Durston, John W.,
Abstract: Aims to demonstrate that the peasantry, while also a category of agricultural producers, may be best understood as a social class. A large part of typically peasant economic behaviour is due to the socio-economic relations maintained with other more powerful classes. As a social class, the peasantry also has its own subculture which strengthens and consolidates its own social institutions. Argues that this subculture is a necessary element in determining the reasons for the current survival of the Latin American peasantry in the framework of 'modernization' of rural structures and of the social mechanisms of surplus appropriation.-from Author © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: S., Molina, S.
Title: Poverty: description and analysis of policies for overcoming it ( Latin America).
Authors with affiliations: Molina, S.,
Abstract: The magnitude and characteristics of poverty in Latin America are traced, and it is concluded that economic growth is a necessary but not sufficient factor for overcoming it, while State action is essential. Distinguishes between two types of policies: the 'distributive' policies alter the primary distribution of income resulting from the structure of ownership and the operation of the economic system, and their application is essential for overcoming the root causes of poverty; 'redistributive' policies correct the primary distribution through transfers of income and goods and services among the different population groups. Both types of policy complement one another, and the manner and extent to which they are combined will depend on the situation of each country.-from Author © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: L., Willmore, L.
Title: Energy demand in Chilean manufacturing.
Authors with affiliations: Willmore, L.,
Abstract: Employs regression analysis to explain inter-industry variation in the energy intensity of production as a function of four variables: change in industry output, substitution of electricity for other fuels, change in employment of labour, and the survival of establishments. The first section provides a brief description of the available data on energy consumption and manufacturing production in Chile. The specific variables used and the estimated equations are described in the next two sections. The main empirical findings are summarized in a concluding section.-from Author © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: R., Prebisch, R.
Title: A historical turning point for the Latin American periphery.
Authors with affiliations: Prebisch, R.,
Abstract: Recognises the existence of serious conjunctural problems: the reduction in the economic growth rate, the high rate of unemployment, the deterioration of the terms of trade, the high level of external indebtedness, etc., which call for the application of a rapid and effective short-term policy; outlines its principal measures. Suggests that industrialisation should be promoted within a regional framework in order to surmount the limits of national markets and the restrictions resulting from the present relationship with the centres. In order to overcome the internal imbalance emphasises that the problems of accumulation, redistribution, and inflation call for the macroeconomic regulation of the surplus: the cost of the crisis and of the reactivation must be spread out equitably, and the labour force must share in the surplus and in the responsibility for accumulation.-from Author © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.
Author Keywords: Indebtedness; Surplus; Terms Of Trade; Unemployment
Index Keywords: indebtedness; surplus; terms of trade; unemployment

Authors: N.E., Garcia, N. E.
Title: Growing labour absorption with persistent underemployment.
Authors with affiliations: Garcia, N. E.,
Abstract: Argues that the substantial and increasing difference in resource requirements per employed person between modern activities and traditional agricultural activities, together with the rapid growth of the non-agricultural economically active population (EAP), the small initial importance of the modern strata, and the slow rate of job retention in modern agricultural activities largely explain why even those countries which show accumulation and economic growth are unable to absorb the entire transfer of labour from the agricultural sector to the modern segments. As a result, concludes that it is a problem not only of the size of capital formation, but also of the limited effects of this capital formation, and the pressures of the urban labour supply. Thus, what is relevant is not only the size but also the composition of the use of resources and their greater or lesser homogenizing effects.-from Author © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: E., Ortega, E.
Title: Peasant agriculture in Latin America: situations and trends.
Authors with affiliations: Ortega, E.,
Abstract: Demonstrates that the peasant phenomenon still exists in most of the countries of the region, and peasant families working small agricultural units represent a significant percentage of the population of Latin America. They play an important role in the functioning of agriculture and the economy and make a significant contribution to production and to both the food and labour markets. The peasantry is not isolated from society, and because of the physical, economic and cultural integration processes at work, any exclusion or omission of the factors regarding the peasantry distorts the understanding of social phenomena.-from Author © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: N., Islam, Nurul
Title: Latin American agriculture: its prospects up to the end of the century.
Authors with affiliations: Islam, Nurul,
Abstract: Latin American agriculture has not kept pace with the greater demand from the growth of the population and of income. Maintains that it is necessary to change these trends by increasing the cultivable area, improving yields, securing a relative reduction in agricultural imports, and making changes in policies and institutions. These policy changes should be directed towards increasing production and distributing equitably the benefits of development among all social groups and regions. -from Author © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.
Author Keywords: Food Production; Policy Changes

Authors: H., Kirsch, H.
Title: The participation of youth in the development process of Latin America: problems and policies regarding labour force insertion, education and employment opportunities.
Authors with affiliations: Kirsch, H.,
Abstract: The resurgence of interest in the problems of youth has spread most recently to Latin America as a consequence of high rates of unemployment among youth, extensive school desertion, increased delinquency, and increasing rejection of the existing social order by young people in the secondary and higher levels of education in certain countries. On the basis of the few empirical studies carried out in Latin America, it examines the situation and needs of youth from three vantage points: youth as a category of analysis and object of policy and planning; the insertion of youth into the labour force; and the interaction between education and employment possibilities.-from Author © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: L.L., Cordovez, L. L.
Title: Trends and recent changes in the Latin American food and agriculture situation.
Authors with affiliations: Cordovez, L. L.,
Abstract: Analyses the chief trends and recent changes and seeks to give an overall picture, despite limitations arising from the insufficient and sometimes partial data. The economic progress achieved is obvious, since the dimensions of the sector increased by a factor of 1.4 during the 1970s. The technical progress is also evident but uneven. These two forms of progress have been based both on stimuli resulting from public policy and on attractive, although selective, conditions in expanding markets. To a great extent, the expansion achieved in production was made possible by accelerated capital formation in entrepreneurial-type production units. The coexistence of this material progress with continuing rural poverty is the most noteworthy negative feature of Latin American agriculture.-from Author © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: P., Sainz, P.
Title: Adjustment, redeployment or transformation? Background and options in the current situation ( Latin America).
Authors with affiliations: Sainz, P.,
Abstract: Presents a brief description of the problems facing governments in Latin America under the current circumstances. Also outlines two prototypes of policy options based on whether the crisis is considered to be conjunctural or structural in nature. Finally, examines certain elements pertaining to economic dynamism, income distribution, external economic relations, and the sectoral structure that should provide the framework within which economic policies for the situation may be outlined.-from Author © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: R., Brignol, R.; J., Crispi, J.
Title: The peasantry in Latin America: a theoretical approach.
Authors with affiliations: Brignol, R., ; Crispi, J.,
Abstract: Describes the position of the Latin American peasant within a context of dependent capitalism and presents certain criteria for defining the term 'peasant units'. Analyses the way peasant units function and the ways in which they resist disintegration. Finally, hypothesizes that the peasantry will remain in existence because of its complementary role in the expansion of capitalism, and that peasant forms of production in Latin America are not uniform, but rather depend on specific conditions.-from Authors © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: D., Dunham, David
Title: On the history and political economy of small-farmer policies.
Affiliations: International Institute of Social Studies, The Hague, Netherlands
Authors with affiliations: Dunham, David, International Institute of Social Studies, The Hague, Netherlands
Abstract: Part I examines small-farmer policies in an historical perspective, and seeks to show that these policies are not the new phenomena they are sometimes supposed to be, and that their history has been intrinsically connected with the contradictions in particular societies. Part II deals with contemporary policies and argues that, far from constituting a radical break with the past, 'small-farmer' policies have tended to be extremely conventional, preoccupied not so much with the needs of the poor as with the needs of political stability and economic expansion of the capitalist sector. The final part attempts to show how the interests of capitalist groups are strengthened by small-farmer programmes and their elaboration through conventional planning procedures.-from Author © 2018 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: S., Dell, Sidney
Title: On being grandmotherly; the evolution of IMF conditionality.
Authors with affiliations: Dell, Sidney,
Abstract: Analyses the principle of conditionality in order to bring out its limitations and defects: the questionable concept of 'mismanagement', the stress laid on monetary criteria, the placement of responsibility for solving disequilibria onto the deficit countries, the lack of concern shown to establishing the origin of the deficits, and the imposition of stereotyped stabilization programmes in varying situations.-from Author © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.
Author Keywords: Aid; Conditionality; Stabilization Programmes

Authors: C.A., Miro, C. A.; D., Rodriguez, D.
Title: Capitalisim and population in Latin American agriculture: recent trends and problems.
Authors with affiliations: Miro, C. A., ; Rodriguez, D.,
Abstract: On the basis of a body of empirical research the authors explore the relationship between agrarian structure and population, and describe the process of penetration of capitalist forms into agriculture. After emphasizing and demonstrating that this process adopts a variety of forms in different countries and regions, they describe the relationships between some demographical variables, especially fertility and migrations. Suggests future studies.-from Authors © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Authors: A.E., Calcagno, A. E.; J.M., Jakobowicz, J. M.
Author full names: Calcagno, A. E. (7004139250); Jakobowicz, J. M. (6504626986)
Title: Some aspects of the international distribution of industrial activity.
Authors with affiliations: Calcagno, A. E., ; Jakobowicz, J. M.,
Abstract: Examines recent changes in industrial structure at the international level. Attempts to determine the extent of relocation to establish whether this is an almost unfulfilled possibility or a fully implemented process. Describes industrialization in developing countries (DCs) and then examines the 'industrial redeployment' of the developed countries, considering the contradiction that exists between current unemployment and a possible labour shortage between 1985 and 2000. Considers comparative advantages which may induce transnational corporations to establish in DCs and analyses wage differences as weighted by productivity. Policy alternatives are proposed for DCs, comparing the characteristics and effects of 'open' industrialization based on comparative advantages - which would fit in with the industrial 'redeployment' of the developed countries - with the characteristics and effects of a form of industrialization which tends to affirm national autonomy and to supply the majority of the population. -Journal summary International Trade and Development Division of CEPAL. © 2017 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.
